topic: Why the sky is blue and sunsets are red
lesson: Blue light is knocked sideways by air molecules far more than red light, so blue arrives from the whole sky by day, and at sunset the light crosses so much air that the blue has all been scattered away before it reaches you.

post.caption:
Blue light bounces off air molecules far more easily than red light does. By day that scattered blue reaches you from the whole sky. At sunset the light travels through so much more air that the blue is scattered away entirely, and what is left over is red.
